items.text: Jonathan Taylor was limited in practice this week. He hasn't been ruled out, but watch Friday's report before Sunday's game against Miami.
Jared Goff and Amon-Ra St. Brown were both limited in practice ahead of Sunday morning’s game against New England in Munich (9:30 AM ET kickoff, so lineups lock early).
Josh Jacobs still isn’t practicing. Chris Brooks was limited, so Green Bay’s backfield is a committee again this week.

Thursday night: Cam Skattebo is back from his hamstring injury and expected to be a full go, so the model projects him again and trims Devin Singletary's carries. Treylon Burks (foot) is also expected to return for Washington; center Lucas Patrick and TE Colson Yankoff are out.
Patrick Mahomes (elbow) was a full participant in Wednesday practice, so he is on track to start Sunday at Atlanta.
TreVeyon Henderson (illness) has been ruled out again, and Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) did not practice. A.J. Brown and Hunter Henry were limited. The Patriots play Detroit in Munich.
Puka Nacua (knee, toe) did not practice and faces a multi-week absence, though he isn't officially on IR yet.
Rookie WR Carnell Tate (shoulder) and RB Tyjae Spears (knee) did not practice Wednesday. Both missed Week 8 before the bye.
Jakobi Meyers (ankle) and Bhayshul Tuten (ankle, foot) did not practice Wednesday after playing through their injuries last week.
T.J. Hockenson (wrist, chest) and Jauan Jennings (calf) were listed as non-participants on Minnesota's estimated report after Monday night's game.

Kansas City got WR Josh Downs from the Colts for 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks. Downs had 33 catches for 354 yards in nine games for Indianapolis; the model now projects him with the Chiefs, and Indianapolis' other receivers pick up his targets.

Thursday night: J.J. McCarthy (hip), Cam Skattebo (hamstring) and Darnell Mooney (chest) were all full participants Tuesday, and Malik Nabers (knee) has practiced fully all week. For Washington, center Lucas Patrick (concussion) hasn't practiced.
Patrick Mahomes (elbow) is expected to practice in full, putting him on track to start Sunday at Atlanta.

TreVeyon Henderson has missed two games after a hospital stay for unexplained neurological symptoms and could sit again Sunday against Detroit in Germany. With Rhamondre Stevenson also out, Corey Kiner would lead the backfield.

Denver landed LB Daiyan Henley from the Chargers in a rare deadline trade inside the division. He'd played 87% of the Chargers' defensive snaps in Week 9, so the model counts him as missing for Los Angeles.

Lamar Jackson (thumb surgery) is likely out for the rest of the regular season and Tyler Huntley is done for the year, so Jacoby Brissett starts Monday against the Chargers. The model has Brissett as Baltimore's starter the rest of the way.
Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the season with blood clots, so Joe Milton III stays the starter coming out of this week's bye. The model now lowers Philadelphia's receivers to match.
Sam Darnold is expected back in Week 12, after Seattle's Week 11 bye. Drew Lock starts Sunday at Las Vegas.
David Montgomery (groin) hasn't played since Week 5 but hopes to practice soon. When he's back, expect Woody Marks' carries to shrink.
Davante Adams (hamstring surgery) is on IR with a return targeted shortly after the Rams' Week 11 bye. With Puka Nacua also out, the Rams are thin at receiver Sunday at Arizona.
Mike Evans (Achilles tendinitis, ribs) is unlikely to practice Wednesday and hasn't played since Week 6. Deebo Samuel (hamstring) is on track to practice.

Dolphins put QB Malik Willis on injured reserve with a groin injury, so he misses at least Weeks 10 to 13. Kyle McCord, a 2025 sixth-round pick, is in line for his first NFL start Sunday at Indianapolis. The model now rates Miami with McCord through Week 13.

Bills 23, Vikings 6. Buffalo controlled the ball for 42 minutes and forced three Minnesota turnovers; Carson Wentz and the Vikings managed 178 yards and two field goals. The model's locked pick, Buffalo at 56%, won. Its spread side (Vikings +3.5) and total (Over 45.5) both lost.
items.src: Final score and team stats, Nov 9

items.text: Minnesota traded a 2027 third-round pick to Las Vegas for Kirk Cousins, two days after Carson Wentz went 8 of 25 against Buffalo. Cousins is expected to start Sunday at Green Bay, and the model now uses him as the Vikings' starter, which moves that game toward Minnesota. Rookie Fernando Mendoza takes over in Las Vegas.

San Francisco got WR Keenan Allen from Indianapolis for a 2027 sixth-round pick. Allen leads the Colts with 40 catches. He's moved to the 49ers in the projections; his numbers there use his Colts role, so they're rough until he plays a game in San Francisco.
Buffalo filled its safety need with Amani Hooker from Tennessee.
Cincinnati called off its agreed trade for Eagles edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie over the compensatory-pick formula. He stays in Philadelphia.
DT Zach Sieler needs season-ending biceps surgery.
Good news for the Chargers: imaging on Justin Herbert's left middle finger came back negative, with no fracture.
Patrick Mahomes (right elbow strain) and Xavier Worthy (hamstring) are day-to-day. The model still has Mahomes starting at Atlanta.
Garrett Wilson is in the concussion protocol and must clear it to play Buffalo.
Guard Sean Rhyan is out at least a month with a high ankle sprain, and Josh Jacobs needs surgery on a fractured finger. Both count against Green Bay.

WR Michael Wilson is out for the season with a fractured vertebra, suffered on Arizona's fourth offensive play against Seattle. He had 51 catches for 546 yards and was on pace for a second straight 1,000-yard season. He's off the fantasy rankings, and his snaps count against Arizona.

Gardner Minshew likely tore the UCL in his throwing arm and may need season-ending surgery. Rookie Carson Beck is expected to start Sunday against the Rams. With no NFL passing history, the model rates him as a typical new starter, which lowers Arizona's chances.
Rhamondre Stevenson is expected to miss time with a knee tendon issue. He's off the fantasy rankings for Week 10.

Puka Nacua has MCL and PCL sprains in his right knee plus turf toe, and Sean McVay says he'll likely go on injured reserve. That means at least four games; with the Week 11 bye, Dec. 20 at Dallas is the earliest return. He's out of the fantasy rankings and his snaps now count in the Rams' injury load.
items.src: Larry Brown Sports (via NFL Network), Nov 9

items.text: Jacksonville made three defensive trades in one day: DT Jordan Davis from Philadelphia (2027 first-round and 2029 second-round picks), S Jessie Bates from Atlanta (2027 second, 2028 fifth) and DT Davon Godchaux from New Orleans. Their old teams now count them as missing; Jacksonville’s ratings catch up as they play.

TE Jake Ferguson and RB Tyler Goodson will miss multiple weeks, and S P.J. Locke is out for Sunday against San Francisco, per Brian Schottenheimer. George Pickens and Kavontae Turpin are among those to be decided later in the week.
Detroit acquired S Andre Cisco from the Jets for a 2028 sixth-round pick.
Deshaun Watson cleared the concussion protocol and is expected to start Sunday against Houston. The model now uses Watson instead of Shedeur Sanders.

Mike Macdonald ruled Sam Darnold out for Sunday at Las Vegas; he's still recovering from quad and rib injuries and could return after the Week 11 bye. Drew Lock starts again, playing through an oblique injury. If Lock can't go, rookie Jalen Milroe is next.
J.J. McCarthy has a hip pointer but is expected to play Thursday against Washington. RB Cam Skattebo should be back from his hamstring injury.
Josh Jacobs is expected to miss up to three weeks. He's removed from projections, and his snaps now count in Green Bay's injury load.
items.src: Yahoo Sports NFL live updates, Nov 9

items.text: A.J. Brown has missed two games; the Patriots plan for him to travel to Germany for Sunday's game against Detroit, with no final decision. Lineman Ben Brown won't make the trip.
The deadline passed with Jonathan Taylor still a Colt; Indianapolis reportedly turned down second-round picks. He stays the Colts' workhorse, now with Keenan Allen gone to San Francisco.
items.src: USA TODAY Sports via Yahoo, Nov 10
